Three symptoms show up most consistently across the IACI conditions. First, fatigue that rest does not fix: a baseline exhaustion that persists even with adequate sleep, and that worsens with activity in a way ordinary deconditioning doesn't explain. Second, cognitive impairment, often called brain fog: trouble concentrating, memory problems, a general mental slowness that wasn't there before the infection. Third, and most distinctive, post-exertional malaise, or PEM: a disproportionate worsening of symptoms that characteristically hits twelve to seventy-two hours after physical, cognitive, or emotional exertion, and can last for days or weeks. A person might take a short walk, feel fine immediately afterward, then become profoundly fatigued a day or two later. PEM is the symptom that links long COVID most directly to ME/CFS.
